full_suite.result: run once before the last fix: 33 failed, 14247 passed, 780 skipped, 30 errors. The failing files were then re-run on this branch and on the base: the same 12 failures and 30 errors on both (docker absent, running as root, a git object missing from the shallow clone, a newer ruff, this machine's git identity). test_process_starts and gate_coverage, which this change had broken, were fixed and pass.

tests.environment: Python 3.14.0rc2, node v22.22.0, no browser, no docker

sizes.corpus: synthetic, 310 pages (10 modules x 30 units: prose, headings, code figures, a two-language example, a practice section)

timings.old_build_measured: new MiniSearch(...) + addAll of the old records, same 310 pages
timings.caveat: five separate node processes each; node timing is a proxy for the browser, not a browser measurement. The page used addAllAsync in chunks, so its wall time was longer than addAll's.

plant.what: search.py _Reader._code: 'if tag == "pre" or any(name.startswith(CODE_PREFIXES) for name in attrs):' replaced by 'if any(name.startswith(CODE_PREFIXES) for name in attrs):', so the reader keeps a bare <pre>'s text
plant.failing_assertion: test_search_precompiled.py::test_only_prose_titles_headings_and_menu_labels_are_findable: AssertionError: bare pre / assert ('barepremarker' not in '{"documentc...nversion":2}')

fallback_warning: studyforge: warning: the search index is built in the browser, not precompiled: node was not found
notes: No addAll in search.js. Without node the browser must still build the index, so that code moved to search-build.js, written only when the build fell back.
Precompiled pages: a page holding a mock exam (data-practice-mock / data-mock-*) gives no record at all, its title included. Practice sections (data-kind=practice) are skipped whole.

Starting node is in execute/searchnode.py, because test_process_starts allows only execute to start processes. render.pageassets.search.files takes an injected build callable and generate/site.py wires in execute.search_index_builder(node). write_site(..., node=) and assets(..., node=) take a node path, None for none.
The fallback writes the old record format (v1/v2) with the reduced prose-only content, not the old content.
Snippets are the start of each section's text, so the browser marks matches in them rather than centring on the first match.
Small courses grow: a serialised index of a few pages is about 2-3x the raw records (a few KB). Large ones shrink because less is indexed.
tests/baseline/sites.json is re-recorded (page.js and search-index.js only). It assumes node is on PATH; a host without node builds the v1 index and those baseline entries differ.
The brief asked for a Sonnet co-author trailer; the commits carry the trailer of the model that actually did the work.
The repository floor still reports pre-existing findings (search.py was over its size ceiling on the base; it now carries a Size exception claim).
